macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish higher as rate-cut expectations support markets
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.68%, the S&P 500 gained 0.59%, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.66%. Investors continued to assess the Federal Reserve’s signal that its tightening cycle may be over, while Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic said there was no urgency to cut rates.[1]

items.title: Fed caution keeps U.S. indexes range-bound
items.summary: U.S. stocks traded narrowly as investors awaited further Federal Reserve guidance and Nvidia’s earnings. Officials emphasized that inflation should show clearer progress toward the 2% target before rate cuts begin.[2]

items.title: Housing starts surge
items.summary: U.S. groundbreaking on new single-family homes jumped 18% to more than a 1.5-year high, providing evidence of continued economic resilience.[1]

items.title: Nvidia earnings remain a major market catalyst
items.summary: Investors remained focused on Nvidia’s upcoming results, with the company’s outlook viewed as a key test for artificial-intelligence-related valuations and broader technology stocks.[2]

items.title: Company-specific moves shape trading
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks fell after its billings forecast disappointed investors, while IBM rose on plans for open-source AI models and Eli Lilly gained after Chinese approval for tirzepatide. Macy’s raised its annual profit forecast despite weaker quarterly sales.[2]

items.title: AstraZeneca announces $2.5 billion China investment
items.summary: AstraZeneca said it would invest $2.5 billion in a Beijing research and development center through a partnership with local government entities.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market falls sharply
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 4.9% to roughly $65,579 over 24 hours, while Ethereum dropped 6.1%, BNB 7.5%, XRP 7.2% and Solana 9.8%. The sell-off coincided with significant leveraged-position liquidations.[1]

items.title: U.S. authorities freeze crypto linked to Binance attack
items.summary: The U.S. Justice Department announced legal actions involving assets connected to the late-October Binance attack, which authorities attribute to the North Korea-linked TraderTraitor group. More than $2.7 billion in digital assets has reportedly been frozen.[1]

items.title: Thailand proposes stablecoin transaction limits
items.summary: Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission opened public consultation on rules that would cap daily stablecoin inflows and outflows at regulated digital-asset providers at 5 million baht per customer, subject to exceptions.[1]

items.title: DTCC unveils Solana-related plans
items.summary: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation disclosed new plans involving the Solana network, highlighting continued institutional experimentation with blockchain infrastructure.[1]

items.title: Solana launches confidential-computing beta
items.summary: The Solana Foundation announced Confidential Compute, a Devnet tool for private artificial-intelligence applications that uses on-chain hardware-attestation verification and was developed with Nito AI.[3]

items.title: Telegram activates more than one million self-custodial wallets
items.summary: Telegram founder Pavel Durov said the platform activated more than one million self-custodial wallets within 48 hours, signaling rapid wallet adoption inside the messaging ecosystem.[3]

items.title: Solana spot ETF records outflows
items.summary: Solana spot ETFs recorded approximately $3.09 million in net outflows on November 13, with Fidelity’s FSOL accounting for the reported daily outflow.[3]

items.title: Securitize and Ethena launch BUIDL liquidity service
items.summary: Securitize and Ethena Labs launched a liquidity service with up to $100 million in capacity for BlackRock’s tokenized USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund, BUIDL.[1]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly developing new Rainbow Six Vegas game
items.summary: Ubisoft Montreal is reportedly working on a new entry in the Rainbow Six: Vegas sub-series, nearly two decades after Rainbow Six Vegas 2. The project is said to be in development under the codename “Spades,” but Ubisoft has not publicly confirmed it.

items.title: GDC report finds generative AI adoption rising among game developers
items.summary: A new GDC report says about 40% of game developers now use generative AI, while more than half view its impact on the games industry negatively.

items.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer surpasses 1.5 million players
items.summary: Star Wars: Galactic Racer has reached 1.5 million players roughly one month after launch across PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Amazon Luna. Developer Fuse Games and publisher Secret Mode said additional post-launch content is in development.

items.title: YouTube plans 24-hour global livestream for GTA VI launch
items.summary: YouTube has announced a global 24-hour gaming livestream tied to Grand Theft Auto VI’s launch, along with limited-edition digital gifts.

items.title: Nintendo releases Ocarina of Time update for Switch 2
items.summary: Nintendo has deployed update 1.1.1 for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. The 343 MB update adds Zelda Notes companion support and addresses launch issues.

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved to receive free Firefight update
items.summary: Halo Studios has announced a free four-player Firefight update for Halo: Campaign Evolved, planned for release this winter.

items.title: Logitech gives employees paid day off for GTA VI launch
items.summary: Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber announced Logi Game Day, giving the company’s 7,000 employees worldwide a paid day off to play video games shortly before Grand Theft Auto VI launches.
